chapter: Jazz club letters and Dr. Sushan
title: Dr. Sushan's 1949 letter about the Hammersmith Palais anniversary
summary: A December 1949 letter from Dr. Edmond Souchon conveys Lord Donegal's invitation to a London celebration and says only one ODJB started it all.

blocks.x: No. It's going now. This is a letter. At the head is Dr. Admiral Sushaw, New Orleans. They, December 29, 1949. Dear Mr. LaRock, resuming our conversation of last night, I would simply write to repeat. The Marcus of Donegal wrote me and asked me to communicate to you. His address is, the Marcus of Donegal, 16 High Park Gate, London, SWF, England. As you know, Lord Donegal is head of all the jazz clubs of Great Britain. They're planning to have a 30-year centennial commemorating the opening up of the original Dixie Land Jazz Band in Hammersmith's Palais. On the exact same date you fellas opened up 30 years ago. It is going to be a national celebration of some sorts, and they would like to have you as a guest for the occasion. They would not ask you to play unless they wish you to play. I don't think they know that you are a very married man, but I will tell Lord Donegal of your fine wife and children, and I feel sure that he will include her in the invitation. Lord Donegal would like you to write him as soon as you can and answer all the above information. Also, would you give him the exact date that you opened up, so they can plan their celebration on that exact date. He also expresses his desire to borrow some old photographs of the old gang for them to use both for publicity, etc. The reason I am writing all these details is that I want you and Lord Donegal to deal with each other directly, and I don't want to become involved as a third party. However, if I can be of any assistance, don't hesitate to call on me. Please count on me as fully realizing the important position which you, which is underlying you, occupy as a member of the Pioneer Band and what you and your group has done for New Orleans. There is no confusion in my mind between white music and colored music, nor the relative merits of each. There never was and never will be any but one ODJB that started the whole thing. Sincerely, Edmond Sushan, M.D.
